name: Reality Model Blueprint
blueprint_identity: Reality Model Blueprint is an original operating blueprint designed to convert a known strategy, business, product, execution, or operations problem into a controlled sequence of diagnosis, decision, execution, feedback, and adaptation.
what_it_solves: Unclear business model assumptions
Static planning that never turns into evidence
Misalignment between value creation, delivery, and revenue capture
trigger_conditions: A user starts a new business, product, service, or monetization idea
A project has unclear customer, offer, channel, or revenue logic
Execution is happening but the business model is not producing measurable traction
operating_sequence: Map the core value exchange: who receives value, what they receive, and why it matters.
Identify all assumptions behind customer demand, delivery, pricing, channel, and retention.
Score each assumption as proven, partially proven, or unproven.
Convert the weakest assumptions into proof actions such as outreach, prototype testing, pricing tests, or delivery experiments.
Update the model after evidence is collected and remove unsupported parts.
adaptation_rules: If customer proof is weak, the blueprint shifts from growth to validation.
If revenue proof is weak, pricing and offer tests become priority.
If delivery proof is weak, system setup and fulfillment tasks become priority.
success_indicators: A complete business model exists with evidence attached to each core part.
The project can explain who it serves, what it sells, how it delivers, and how money moves.
The next tasks directly test or strengthen the weakest business assumptions.
failure_controls: Blocks scaling when demand is unproven.
execution_logic_summary: When Reality Model Blueprint activates, it should not produce passive analysis. It must create a visible decision path and a next-action set. The blueprint should remain active until the core problem it solves is either proven resolved, moved into another blueprint, or blocked by failed evidence. Its main job is to reduce guesswork and force execution to follow reality.
